properties.inline_policies: Inline policy documents encoded as JSON strings on the principal.
properties.collected: Whether the account was targeted by collection.

identity.AWS_Account: The node identifier is the account root ARN: `arn:aws:iam::<account-id>:root`. This ARN also identifies the account environment.
identity.AWS_S3Object: The node identifier is the object ARN: `arn:aws:s3:::<bucket>/<key>`. The key is part of the identifier, including any path separators.
identity.AWS_Resource: The node identifier is the discovered resource ARN. The collector uses a deterministic identifier derived from name, kind, account, and region only when an AWS node has no ARN.

nodes.AWS_Group: IAM groups supply policies to their members. Effective permission edges are projected from IAM users and roles, rather than treating the group as an authenticating identity.
nodes.AWS_S3Bucket: An object-operation edge ending at this bucket describes the modeled object namespace. It does not assert permission on every concrete object key. Object collection can also produce edges to individual S3 objects.
nodes.AWS_EKSCluster: IRSA and Pod Identity edges summarize workload access from the cluster to IAM roles. Review the service-account scope and trust conditions before interpreting access for a particular workload. Kubernetes node kinds belong to a separate extension and are outside this AWS schema inventory.
nodes.AWS_SSMParameter: The node contains parameter metadata. The collector does not put the parameter value in these properties.

edges.AWS_HasSCP: The emitted direction is from an account to a service control policy that applies directly or through inheritance. The schema description uses “Organization”; the collector projects this relationship onto affected accounts.
edges.AWS_HasRCP: The emitted direction is from an account to a resource control policy that applies directly or through inheritance. The schema description uses “Organization”; the collector projects this relationship onto affected accounts.
edges.AWS_HasExternalRoleTrust: The source is the account containing the trusting role. The destination is the external account trusted by that role. This summarizes cross-account trust; it does not itself establish effective permission to assume the role.
edges.AWS_CanAssumeRole: The collector projects an authorized STS assumption to the target role. Trust and identity/resource-policy evaluation determine whether the request is allowed. A trust declaration alone is represented by AWS_Trusts/AWS_TrustedBy and is not equivalent to this capability.
edges.AWS_CanGetFederationToken: This is a self-edge on the IAM user. The destination is the same user, rather than another principal or a newly created federated-user node.
edges.AWS_CanGetSessionToken: This is a self-edge: the source and destination identify the same IAM user or role. It does not grant control over a different principal.
edges.AWS_CanAssumeRoleWithSAML: The source is the SAML provider trusted by the role. The collector derives this direction from a same-account federated trust statement allowing `sts:AssumeRoleWithSAML`. Trust conditions remain on the assumption edge; this does not say that any IAM principal can obtain a valid SAML assertion.
edges.AWS_CanAssumeRoleWithWebIdentity: The source is the OIDC provider trusted by the role. The collector derives this direction from a same-account federated trust statement allowing `sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`. Trust conditions remain on the assumption edge; access depends on the token and its claims.
edges.AWS_CanPassRoleToService: The collector requires `iam:PassRole` on a concrete role in the same account, at least one supported service-operation bundle, and suitable service trust or a supported trust-rewrite path. It excludes passing a role to itself. `services` records existing service trust; `services_via_trust_rewrite` records alternatives requiring `iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy`. The 13 AWS_CanPassRoleVia… relationships retain individual route evidence. Inspect `methods` for selected operations and conditions.
edges.AWS_CanCreateAndAssociateEKSAccessEntry: The collector combines `eks:CreateAccessEntry` and `eks:AssociateAccessPolicy` for the same collected cluster in the same account. Authorization also uses a representative access-entry ARN. `authorization_targets` and `authorization_actions` retain this distinction from the cluster graph endpoint.
edges.AWS_CanCreateEKSPodIdentityAssociation: The collector requires `eks:CreatePodIdentityAssociation` on a collected cluster, `iam:PassRole` for the destination role, and trust for `pods.eks.amazonaws.com` (or wildcard service trust). It checks `iam:PassedToService` condition evidence and excludes the source role itself. The graph destination is the role; `cluster_arns` records the clusters used for authorization.
edges.AWS_CanCreateEKSNodegroup: Authorization is evaluated on at least one existing cluster, but the emitted destination is its account. This is non-traversable creation evidence. Passing a node role also requires the EKS node-group PassRole route.
edges.AWS_EC2CanVolumeSwap: The collector requires all four volume-swap permissions in the same account and a collected instance with an EBS-backed root volume. It suppresses this composite when that resource-state requirement is not met.
edges.AWS_SSMCanSendCommand: The destination must be a collected, SSM-managed EC2 instance in the same account as the source principal. Authorization alone does not satisfy the managed-instance requirement.
edges.AWS_SSMCanStartSession: The destination must be a collected, SSM-managed EC2 instance in the same account as the source principal. Authorization alone does not satisfy the managed-instance requirement.
edges.AWS_CanGetParameter: For a customer-key-encrypted SecureString parameter, the collector also requires effective `kms:Decrypt` on the key in the SSM service context. It combines the condition evidence. This data-access projection is limited to the same account.
edges.AWS_CanPutParameter: For a customer-key-encrypted SecureString parameter, the collector also requires effective `kms:Encrypt` on the key in the SSM service context. It combines the condition evidence. This data-access projection is limited to the same account.
edges.AWS_CanAssumeRoleViaIRSA: The collector matches the cluster OIDC issuer to a role trust statement. `irsa_subject`, `irsa_subject_operator`, `irsa_audience`, and `is_scoped` preserve service-account scope; review them before applying this cluster-level capability to a workload.
edges.AWS_CanAssumeRoleViaPodIdentity: The collector derives this edge from a collected Pod Identity association with a known cluster ARN and destination role. The relationship summarizes the association at cluster scope.
edges.AWS_Contains: The source is a containing organization, account, or bucket. The endpoint table lists actual containment pairs rather than allowing every source kind to contain every destination kind.
edges.AWS_NodeGroupHasRole: The destination is the node IAM role recorded on the managed node group. Traversability models access to that role through workloads on the node group; runtime metadata access restrictions still matter.
edges.AWS_ClusterHasNodeGroup: The destination is a managed node group belonging to the source cluster. The model treats cluster administration as a path to node-group workloads; runtime scheduling and metadata access restrictions still matter.
edges.AWS_CanGetObject: A bucket destination represents authorization against the modeled object namespace, not every concrete object key. The collector can also emit this capability on a concrete collected object; namespace coverage can suppress redundant object edges.
edges.AWS_CanGetObjectACL: A bucket destination represents authorization against the modeled object namespace, not every concrete object key. The collector can also emit this capability on a concrete collected object; namespace coverage can suppress redundant object edges.

edges.AWS_CanSelfGrantKMSOps: For a supported customer-managed key, the collector derives this edge from effective `kms:CreateGrant` and retains its condition evidence. `grantable_operations` lists the modeled KMS grant operations. Review the conditions before interpreting which grants are usable; this edge is non-traversable.
edges.AWS_CanCreateOIDCProviderAndAssumeRole: The collector combines provider creation in the account with `iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy` on a concrete role in that account. The graph destination is that existing role. Creating a provider alone is not sufficient; the modeled path also requires a usable federated identity and satisfaction of any retained conditions.
edges.AWS_CanCreateSAMLProviderAndAssumeRole: The collector combines provider creation in the account with `iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy` on a concrete role in that account. The graph destination is that existing role. Creating a provider alone is not sufficient; the modeled path also requires a usable federated identity and satisfaction of any retained conditions.
edges.AWS_CanUpdateSelfPolicy: The destination is the account in which the capability is modeled, rather than a newly created principal or an existing policy object. The collector combines the relevant policy and principal-control evidence; the schema description above identifies the technique. Review `methods` and `composite_components` when present for the selected evidence and conditions.
